Android does not let a launcher see other apps. To show what each app looked like when you left it, Drift needs its optional “Drift previews” accessibility service. It only takes a small screenshot about a second after you use an app, cannot read text, passwords or notifications, skips apps that block screenshots, and keeps pictures on this phone.\n\nIf the switch is greyed out: App info > menu > Allow restricted settings.

How to move around the canvas
Drag the empty canvas with one finger. Double-tap an empty spot to go home and back.
Spread or pinch two fingers. The canvas pans and zooms at the same time.
Tap a card to select it, double-tap to launch. Tap the app list button at the bottom right for all apps.
Long-press a card and drag it. Dragged next to another card it snaps to it; a group moves as one piece. Near the screen edge the canvas scrolls by itself.
With a card selected, pinch on it to resize. The top bar has Center, Group, Preview, Pin and Remove; the round button on the card shows or hides its preview.
Swipe with three fingers to jump to the nearest card in that direction. The two round buttons above the app list button show the overview and recent apps.
1. Long-press an app in the dock.\n2. Choose “Create folder”.\n3. The app becomes the first one in the new folder and the folder opens.
1. Open the folder with a tap.\n2. Tap the “+” tile at the end of the grid.\n3. Pick an app in the list; it appears in the folder.
Remove an app from a folder
1. Long-press the app inside the folder.\n2. Choose “Remove from folder”.\nOr drag it onto the dimmed background outside the folder and confirm. The app is not uninstalled.
Open the folder and tap its name, or long-press the folder in the dock and choose “Rename folder”.
Remove a folder from the dock
1. Long-press the folder in the dock.\n2. Choose “Remove from dock”.\n3. If the folder has apps, confirm. They stay in the app list.

1. Long-press an app; a menu appears.\n2. Without lifting your finger, start moving: the menu closes and a lifted copy follows your finger.\n3. Drop it on another tile to put it there. The order is saved.
Tap an empty dock slot to pick an app for it. Long-press it to choose “Add app” or “Create folder”. A folder with no apps stays in the dock as a tile with “+”; open it and tap “+” to fill it.

Drift itself does not hide system bars, exclude gestures, touch the task stack or call any recents API; it only holds the home role.
Drift is not the selected home app right now, so this report describes the stock setup.\nSelect Drift as home (Settings > Apps > Default apps > Home app) and run it again.

This firmware does not expose the stock recents component. Recents and gestures are then implemented by the manufacturer’s own system UI, and how they behave when another app holds the home role is decided by that firmware, not by the home app.

Stock Quickstep layout: the gesture/recents service lives in %1$s, not in the home app. AOSP keeps it working for any home app through a fallback recents activity in that same package, so with this layout system navigation should not depend on Drift. If it still misbehaves, send this report: that would point to a firmware bug.

The recents package is %1$s but the stock gesture service (QUICKSTEP_SERVICE) is %2$s. So recents and swipe-between-apps here are the manufacturer’s own implementation, tied to its system launcher (%3$s%4$s). Whether that implementation still works when a third-party app holds the home role is a firmware decision. An app cannot add it through its manifest or window code.
